questions.question: Define open dumping.
questions.solution_html:
• Open dumping is the practice of disposing of solid waste in an unregulated and uncontrolled manner
  • where waste is simply thrown onto land or into water bodies without any proper treatment
  • management, or environmental protection measures. (2marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Name two agricultural wastes.

  • Any two (2 marks)

questions.question: Which type of polymers are broken down during hydrolysis?
questions.solution_html:
• Polymers that are broken down during hydrolysis are mainly biodegradable polymers containing
  • hydrolysable bonds. Examples include: Carbohydrates (e.g., starch, cellulose), Proteins, Lipids (fats and
  • oils), Nucleic acids.

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: State one advantage of in-vessel composting.
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages of in-vessel composting include: Faster composting process due to controlled conditions.
  • Better control of temperature, moisture, and aeration. Reduced odour and pest problems, requires
  • less space compared to open methods, can be carried out in all weather conditions, produces uniform
  • and high-quality compost, and minimises environmental pollution. Anyone (2 marks)
questions.final_answer: and high-quality compost, and minimises environmental pollution. Anyone
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is compost?
questions.solution_html:
• Compost is a dark, nutrient-rich, humus-like material formed by the decomposition of organic waste
  • (such as plant residues, kitchen waste, and animal manure) by microorganisms under controlled
  • aerobic conditions.It is commonly used as a natural fertiliser and soil conditioner to improve soil
  • fertility, structure, and water-holding capacity. (2 marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.solution_html:

  • Decomposition of organic matter, Enzymatic action, Heat production, Humus formation, Nutrient
  • recycling.

questions.question: Explain the need for sampling in solid waste management.
questions.solution_html:
• Sampling in solid waste management is important to obtain a representative portion of waste for
  • analysis and planning. Determines waste composition, Estimates quantity and characteristics, Aids in
  • selecting treatment methods, supports system design, Cost estimation, Monitoring and evaluation.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List the advantages of biogas as a waste disposal method.
questions.solution_html:
• List the advantages of biogas as a waste disposal method.
  • Reduces organic waste volume by converting it into useful products - Produces renewable energy
  • (biogas) used for cooking, heating, and electricity - Generates nutrient-rich slurry that can be used as
  • organic fertiliser - Environment-friendly – reduces greenhouse gas emissions and pollution.Controls
  • odour and pathogens during digestion - Reduces dependence on fossil fuels, Low-cost and sustainable
  • for rural and household use
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the environmental significance of waste reduction.
questions.solution_html:
• Conserves natural resources , reduces pollution, decreases landfill use , lowers greenhouse gas
  • emissions , Saves energy , protects ecosystems and biodiversity , promotes sustainability .
questions.final_answer: Conserves natural resources , reduces pollution, decreases landfill use , lowers greenhouse gas

questions.question: Explain in detail about end products of composting.
questions.solution_html:
• Humus (finished compost) – A dark, crumbly, soil-like material rich in nutrients; improves soil fertility
  • structure, and water-holding capacity. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) – Released during microbial respiration.
  • Water (H₂O) – Produced during decomposition and helps maintain moisture. Heat – Generated due
  • to microbial activity, which aids in pathogen destruction. Mineral nutrients – Such as nitrogen
  • phosphorus, potassium, and trace elements in forms available to plants.
questions.final_answer: phosphorus, potassium, and trace elements in forms available to plants
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the composition and properties of biogas.
questions.solution_html:
• Composition of biogas: Methane (CH₄), Carbon dioxide (CO₂), Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S), Hydrogen
  • (H₂), Nitrogen (N₂), and water vapour. Properties of biogas: Combustible gas due to methane content
  • Colourless and odourless (pure form; odour due to H₂S), produces smokeless flame when burned
  • Moderate calorific value, Lighter than air Eco-friendly fuel, reduces pollution and greenhouse gas
  • emissions.
  • Essay Question
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe about the advantages and disadvantages of composting.
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages: Reduces waste volume and decreases landfill burden, Produces nutrient-rich compost
  • that improves soil fertility, Environment-friendly – reduces pollution and greenhouse gas emissions
  • Improves soil structure and water-holding capacity, Recycles organic waste into useful material, Low
  • cost and simple method for waste management, Reduces need for chemical fertilisers.
  • Disadvantages: Slow process – takes weeks to months, requires proper maintenance (moisture
  • aeration, temperature), may produce foul odour if not managed properly. Attracts pests and insects
  • requires space for a composting setup, Not suitable for all types of waste (e.g., plastics, metals).
questions.final_answer: requires space for a composting setup, Not suitable for all types of waste (e.g., plastics, metals)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe the structure and preparation of a compost bin.
questions.solution_html:
• Structure & Types of a Compost Bin: Container/Enclosure – Made of plastic, wood, metal, or concrete
  • Base – Usually open or with drainage to allow excess water to escape and contact with soil organisms
  • Lid/Cover – Layers inside – Alternate layers of organic waste (greens) and dry materials (browns)
  • . Preparation of a Compost Bin
